welcome.label: Welcome · the lakes that weren’t there

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: The Lakes That Weren’t There
parts.body: What is making the square lakes, and will the thing being taken ever come back?

welcome.script:
Welcome, scientists! New week, new case, and this time we’re looking at Florida from space.

[ON SCREEN: 1985]
This is a satellite photo of central Florida from 1985. Mostly green fields and wetlands, with some dark spots.

[ON SCREEN: 2023]
Same place, 2023. Look! Dark square lakes and bare tan patches in new places. Hmm. Lakes don’t usually come in squares.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
What is making them? And is something being taken that won’t come back? Find four clues. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · take it apart (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Hold up a pencil.) This pencil used to be part of the Earth. Really!

The wood grew on a tree. The gray part inside isn’t lead at all. It’s a rock, dug out of the ground.

[ON SCREEN: Take it apart]
In the game, take apart a pencil, a juice box and a Florida orange. Drag each part to where it started. Then take apart something near you and write about it.

Save the orange for last. It has a surprise. Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s hint.

part2.label: Part 2 · refill race (Clue 2)

parts.label: ⏳ Refill race
parts.title: Does it come back?
rows: Drag time forward to 1 million years.
Try the water slow and fast.

part2.script:
(Snap your fingers.) If you use something up, does it come back?

Renewable means it comes back fast enough to keep using, like sunlight. Nonrenewable means it takes millions of years to form.

[ON SCREEN: Refill race]
In the Refill race, use up five resources, then drag time forward. Watch which bars fill back up. Try the water at both pumping speeds.

[ON SCREEN: The dragline]
Right after, meet the giant machine that digs up phosphate rock. Tap every number. Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · two sources (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Hold up two different books.) If I only read one of these, I might miss something.

[ON SCREEN: Two sources]
Dr. Reyes found two sources about the mines. Source A is a mining company’s flyer. Source B is a report by government scientists.

[ON SCREEN: The waste pile]
This giant pile is in Source B. Do you think the flyer mentions it?

Sort every fact: benefit or cost. Then build a claim that’s fair to both sources. That’s your last clue. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Square lakes?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab: what is making those square lakes?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report. Two short answers, a comparison of two Florida resources in Part C, and a CER. Want to draw your chart? That’s a bonus. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Your answers save as you type. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “All renewable resources are good for the environment and all nonrenewable resources are bad.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says all renewables are good and all nonrenewables are bad. Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: The solar farm]
Think about this solar farm. Renewable, yes. But what happened to the land?

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side and two facts from today. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🪨 Your specimen
parts.title: Phosphate pebble
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Florida’s resource map
parts.body: Why are some Florida resources found in one place and not another?

closing.script:
Case closed! The square lakes are old phosphate mine pits, and that rock won’t come back.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a phosphate pebble goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time, we’ll read a map of Florida. Why is phosphate only in one part of the state? Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

part3.label: Part 3 · impact check (Clue 3)
part3.script: Every resource has an impact, even renewable ones. Open each photo, stamp it renewable or nonrenewable, then pick what using it changes. Look closely at the last photo. Have you seen it before? Press Listen.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
